reasons.cron: Every five minutes picks up the next task soon after the previous one is approved without firing idle turns often.

design:
Tier 2. Outward-facing: the Hub acts on a code host's CI result by drafting a PR and sending work back, and a red main must not bounce every build. Migration: adds project columns only (the CI setting, the list of check names, the interval, the cutoff) and build/task columns for the last CI result. Rollback: the columns are read only when the setting is on, so downgrading drops them and those projects fall back to slice 1's local landing checks.

Decisions (operator, 2026-11-06):
- An explicit project setting, not detection.
- The checks that count: GitHub's required checks for the PR's base branch, else a list of check names the project sets. The setting cannot be turned on with nothing to wait for.
- A failure returns the PR to draft and sends back the latest task pushed. With the squash setting, that is still the latest task pushed.
- Only the result for the latest commit counts. A result for a superseded commit decides nothing.
- A counted check that also fails on main's latest commit is not the task's fault: it is shown as 'fails on main too' and sends nothing back. A check with no concluded result on main counts as not failing there; the send-back says so. Test-level matching against the known-failing list, using a report CI uploads, is later work.
- While a counted check is pending, the Hub asks GitHub at an interval the project sets (default 2 minutes, 1-60). It stops when the run finishes, or after a cutoff the project sets (default 60 minutes) with no conclusion, after which only slice 1's actions ask. Slice 1 lists 'a timer that asks GitHub' as a non-goal to reconsider in slices 2 and 3; this is that reconsideration, bounded to pending runs.
- The PR is marked ready only when every task is pushed and CI passed. This replaces slice 1 FR-5's ready condition for these projects.

CURRENT (slice 1)  approved -> local landing checks -> push -> draft PR ... all pushed -> ready
PROPOSED           approved -> push (no local landing checks) -> CI pending -> ask every N minutes (stop at cutoff)
                     passed               -> tasks read as checked; all pushed + passed -> PR ready
                     failed, main green or no result -> PR back to draft; latest task pushed sent back with failing checks + links
                     failed, main red too -> 'fails on main too', nothing sent back, PR stays draft

open_questions.question: Is a CI failure checked against the known-failing list? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): check-level now; a counted check that also fails on main's latest commit is not the task's (FR fails-on-main-too). Test-level matching is later.
Interval and cutoff? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): both are project settings; interval 1-60 minutes, 2 by default; cutoff 60 minutes by default (its 5-1440 range is the author's choice).
A superseded commit's result? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): only the latest commit counts.
Nothing to wait for? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): the setting cannot be turned on, nor a PR build start, with no required checks and an empty list.
Main has no result for the failing check? Answered (operator, 2026-11-06): the task is held responsible and sent back, and the send-back says main had no result.

problem: With slice 1, an approved task of a PR build still runs the project's full landing-phase checks locally before it is pushed (slice 1 FR-3). Then the project's CI runs the same suite again on the PR. That duplicates the most expensive work on the machine the operator is using, which is the cost the roadmap 'Checks cost less on a machine that is in use' exists to cut. A team that works through PRs already trusts its CI as the gate. Today the local landing check is project_checks.configured_checks(project, PHASE_LANDING) run by the landing queue (hub/hub/landing_queue.py:332). The pre-review checks (PHASE_REVIEW) are a different thing: they gate the agent reviewer, not the landing, and this slice leaves them alone.

requirements.statement: A project with PR landing on has a setting 'the PR's CI is the full check', off until the operator turns it on; it cannot be turned on while PR landing is off, and turning PR landing off turns it off.

In a project with the setting on, an approved task of a PR build is pushed without running the project's landing-phase checks locally; its pre-review checks run as before, and a project with the setting off keeps slice 1's local landing checks.

The checks that count for a PR are the status checks GitHub marks required for the PR's base branch; when none are marked required, or the Hub cannot read them, they are the check names listed in the project's setting; the setting cannot be turned on, and a PR build cannot start, while the repository marks no required checks and the list is empty, and the refusal names both.
Only the counted checks' results on the PR's current head commit decide anything; a result on a commit a later push has superseded is shown as superseded and neither passes nor sends back any task.

While any counted check on an open PR's head commit is pending or has not yet reported, the Hub asks GitHub for the result at the project's interval, in addition to slice 1's actions; it stops asking on the interval once every counted check has concluded, the PR is merged or closed, or the project's cutoff has passed since the push with a counted check still unconcluded, in which case the build shows that CI has not finished and only slice 1's actions ask again until the next push.
When every counted check on the head commit succeeds, the build and each task pushed in that head read as checked by CI, naming the commit.

When a counted check on the head commit fails and does not also fail on main, the PR is returned to draft and the latest task pushed is sent back to its builder as a landing failure, naming each such failing check with its link; with the squash setting the latest task pushed is chosen the same way.

In a project with the setting on, the PR is marked ready for review only when every task of the build has been pushed and every counted check on the head commit has succeeded; until then it stays a draft.

The build card and each of its tasks show CI's state on the head commit (pending, passed, failed, failing on main too, superseded, not finished), each counted check with its name, state and link, and when the Hub last asked; a failed ask is shown with GitHub's error.

requirements.rationale: The operator made the cutoff a setting (2026-11-06) because CI duration differs widely between projects; the cutoff's range is the author's choice: 5 minutes is the shortest that outlasts a fast CI run, 24 hours the longest a build should sit unnoticed.
requirements.statement: The project's setting carries the interval between asks while CI is pending, in whole minutes from 1 to 60, 2 by default, and the cutoff after which interval asking stops, in whole minutes from 5 to 1440, 60 by default; a value out of its range, or a cutoff shorter than the interval, is refused on save with a reason naming the rule broken.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-06: with no result on main, the task is held responsible rather than the build waiting, so a build never hangs on main's CI; naming the missing result lets a wrong send-back be spotted.
requirements.statement: Before sending anything back, the Hub reads each failing counted check's result on the latest commit of the project's main branch on GitHub; a check that also failed there is shown on the build as failing on main too and is not the task's; when every failing counted check also fails on main, no task is sent back and the PR stays a draft; a check with no concluded result on main (pending, or never run there) counts as not failing on main, and the send-back says main had no result for it.

in_scope: A project setting, 'the PR's CI is the full check', available when PR landing is on, with a list of check names, an interval and a cutoff
Pushing a PR build's approved tasks without local landing-phase checks in such a project
Choosing which checks count: required checks, else the project's list
Asking GitHub for CI's result on the interval while a counted check is pending, up to the project's cutoff, and on slice 1's actions
Comparing a failing counted check with the same check on main's latest commit
A failing result the task caused: PR back to draft, latest task pushed sent back
Marking the PR ready only when every task is pushed and CI passed
Showing CI's state and each counted check on the build and its tasks
non_goals: Changing the pre-review checks, which still run locally before agent review
Matching individual failing tests from CI against the known-failing list (later; needs a test report CI uploads)
Review comments coming back as send-backs (slice 3)
The Hub re-running, cancelling or configuring CI on the host, or changing branch protection
Waiting for main's own CI run to conclude before judging a PR failure
Builds that land on main or nowhere: their checks are unchanged
PR builds in a project without the setting: slice 1's local landing checks still apply
Switching this repository to PR landing

summary: A project with PR landing on can set that its PR's CI is the full check. Its PR builds then push approved tasks without running the landing-phase checks locally. The Hub reads the result of the checks that count on the PR's head commit: the ones GitHub marks required, else a list the project names. While a run is pending, the Hub asks GitHub at an interval the project sets (2 minutes by default) and stops after a cutoff the project also sets (60 minutes by default) with no conclusion. A failure returns the PR to draft and sends back the latest task pushed, unless the same check also fails on main. The PR is marked ready only when every task is pushed and CI passed. Product, general, opt-in. Tier 2: outward-facing, plus a migration. Builds after slice 1 (a-build-lands-as-one-pull-request).

tasks.description: A drive on a scratch GitHub repository whose workflow has one required check that fails when a marker file is present. It builds a two-task spec with PR landing and the CI setting on. A passing first task leaves the PR a draft until the second; a second task adding the marker returns the PR to draft and sends that task back with the check's link; its fix makes CI pass and the PR ready. It is recorded failing before the build.
